subtopics.title: Convert using exchange rates
subtopics.exposition: Different countries have their own currencies. To find the cost in rands of an amount priced in a foreign currency, use the exchange rate in rands per unit of the foreign currency: with pound 1 = R12.41 a price of pound 4 is R49.64, and with 1 kr = R1.37 a price of 48 kr is R65.76 (the foreign amount multiplied by the rate). To find how much foreign currency a rand amount buys, write down the equation by letting the equivalent amount in the foreign currency (euros) be x. To buy foreign currency with rands, divide the amount of rands by the exchange rate (rands per unit of the foreign currency): x = 10 000 / 10.68 = 936.33 euros. Write the final answer as a sentence stating the amount of foreign currency bought with the rands: Saba can buy euro 936.33 with R10000. An exchange rate is written as one unit of a foreign currency equal to an amount in rands, for example euro 1 = R10.68, pound 1 = R12.41 and 1 kr = R1.37. The three currencies most likely to be seen are the British pound (pound sign), the American dollar ($) and the euro (euro sign).

subtopics.title: Saving or loss from rate change
subtopics.exposition: When the rand is weaker, the same amount of rands buys less of other currencies. The price of oil increases when the South African rand weakens. A currency gets stronger when money is invested in the country. When we buy products imported from other countries we invest money in those countries, and as a result the rand weakens.

subtopics.title: Compare amounts across currencies
subtopics.exposition: Prices of the same item quoted in different currencies (pound 4 in England, R20 in South Africa, 48 kr in Norway) are compared by converting the foreign prices to rands (R49.64 and R65.76), which shows the item costs more in some places than in others.
